exact_claim:
The eventual application provides information, factual checks and draft reference. It cannot constitute a court, issue a punishment, settle contested facts or exercise command discretion. High-risk decisions must remain under a competent commander with JAG advice.

original_title: Scope of this volume and hierarchy of authority
exact_claim:
Military justice involves distinct preliminary, summary disposal and court-martial processes. An officer must establish both personal jurisdiction over the individual and legal authority for each proposed act. A study note does not confer any power.

original_title: Purpose and scope of Volume IV
exact_claim: A court-martial is a legally constituted trial forum distinct from a Court of Inquiry, charge hearing and summary punishment. The lawful forum depends on personal jurisdiction, offence, rank, command, warrant or other authority, date and statutory limits. Record accused service status at relevant dates, present status and effective attachment. Identify every alleged act/omission and Army Act offence, considering civil-offence jurisdiction. Check trial forum, convening competence and any applicable warrants/restrictions. Preserve earlier CoI, Rule 22, SoE and service records without treating those steps as a conviction. RISKS: Substituting unsigned officer summary | invoking expediency without reasons

original_title: 1.3 CoI compared with other proceedings
exact_claim: A CoI collects evidence and may be required to report on identified matters. It does not function as a court-martial. Hearing of charge under Rule 22, Summary of Evidence under Rule 23 and subsequent trial are legally different stages. A CoI finding should not be presented as a conviction or as an automatic substitute for a competent authority's decision. Supreme Court decisions have emphasised the fact-finding character of a CoI and the separateness of the subsequent trial. ['Do not frame guilt as conclusively established by a CoI.', 'Do not assume a CoI is invariably a prerequisite to a court-martial.', 'Do not treat all CoI witness statements as admissible substantive evidence at a trial: see Rule 182.'] []

original_title: Counting interruptions and forfeiture
exact_claim:
Question: What happens to interrupted or forfeited service?
Legal position: PRA Part I distinguishes service that qualifies, interruption/condonation and forfeiture. The actual penalty, break and subsequent restoration must be identified before calculating a final qualifying-service result.
Checks: List all service periods chronologically.; Map interruption/absence/forfeiture orders to governing regulation.; Check condonation authority; do not assume automatic benefit.; Obtain Accounts verification.
Records: Service register; forfeiture/remission records; Accounts verification; condonation correspondence
Risks: Do not count service after a forfeiture without restoration; Do not convert calendar years directly into qualifying-service years

original_title: Judgment treatment and precedent checking
exact_claim: Can a case digest be cited without checking appeal history? original_title: Identify the correct forum
exact_claim: A soldier seeks relief after an adverse service order: where should the case begin? Under s14, AFT is the specialised first-instance adjudicatory forum for defined service matters. A statutory appeal from a court-martial arises under s15. Constitutional review by a High Court remains available under Art 226, but this does not make a writ a substitute for the ordinary forum in every case.  Assessment: Record whether challenge is to service order, court-martial or pure constitutional issue; Read s3(o) inclusion/exclusion and s2 personnel applicability; Match remedy to s14 or s15; Test s21 remedy exhaustion, s22 time issues and territorial Bench; Refer jurisdiction doubt to JAG before filing  Documentation: Impugned order; Service status and rank proof; Petition/reply trail; Complete case chronology  Risks: Blindly directing every grievance to AFT; Filing an OA instead of court-martial appeal; Assuming Art 226 always creates original forum of choice  Example: An officer challenging a non-selection order generally raises service-matter issues; a petition against a GCM conviction engages s15.

original_title: Identify exclusions in service matters

Assessment: Break combined grievance into legally distinct claims; Test each against s3(o)(i)-(iv) exclusions; Determine whether s15 court-martial appeal may independently apply; Research binding decisions in territorial jurisdiction; Record reason for accepting or denying jurisdiction  Documentation: Exact administrative order; Relief requested; Jurisdiction note; Relevant bench precedent  Risks: Treating broad any other matter language as unrestricted; Conflating transfer with promotion; Assuming excluded s14 SCM case necessarily outside s15  Example: Posting challenge and seniority claim in one application require issue-wise forum screening.

original_title: Competent authority and delegation audit
